Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection on the same validation users creates selection optimism; every evaluated checkpoint contributes to search. Nested evaluation or an untouched outer holdout separates selection from assessment; formally reusable holdouts require controlled access, not ordinary repeated scoring ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)). For this pinned benchmark, retain its splits and evaluator, predeclare search/checkpoint limits, log all validation queries, and reserve hidden evaluation for the frozen final choice. Fixed negatives support paired comparison but do not establish full-catalog superiority: sampled metrics can reverse model rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Recommended uncertainty calculation: bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category, resampling 200 users/category and recomputing the equal-weight four-category mean. Report category deltas, macro delta, and a descriptive confidence interval. With these sample sizes, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. This bootstrap conditions on fitted models and fixed candidate sets; it excludes training randomness, candidate-resampling uncertainty, and adaptive winner selection. Bootstrapping the chosen checkpoint does not remove selection bias.

Recommended budgeted protocol: compare SASRec against SASRec plus the proposed residual under matched preprocessing, training seed, candidate sets, checkpoint rules, and explicit GPU-second allocations; charge diagnostics and failures to the 43,200-second budget. Build chronological diagnostic holdouts solely inside public training histories, training separate diagnostic models without those targets or later interactions; respect global cutoffs where feasible, since per-user chronology alone permits cross-user future leakage ([Ji et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060)). Treat these as mechanism checks under a different training regime, not independent confirmation: repeated diagnostic tuning also overfits, and different temporal/catalog conditions can change model rankings.
